_provenance.what: The sources, equations, PDF-set identities and evaluation grid of validation/benchmarks/t5_delta_moment_bound.py -- the n = 2 moment of the gluonic Soffer-type bound applied to LiPolGen's double-helicity-flip structure function Delta(x, Q2) on 6Li (run 2026-10-26 phase C2; docs/benchmarking/08_channel_priority.md sec. 4 ingredient C; docs/benchmarking/04_theory.md sec. 4, T-18).
_provenance.compiled: 2026-10-26, by the phase-C2 worker of run 2026-10-26 (first pass); extended the same day by the second pass of phase C2 (KS20 added; DS16 (3)-(5), LOI18 (6) and the SS90 target state added), after the first pass's numbers had been computed and seen
_provenance.transcription: Each equation under body.sources[*].equations was read where its pages_read says: the bound, the relation and every number this harness uses (DS16 (3)-(5), (9)-(14), (32), (36); SS90 (2.5), (2.11), (2.12), (3.5); LOI18 (6)-(9); CvDM17 (34)-(36); CRSZ25 (2); KS20 (67), (68)) off the page IMAGE (pdftoppm, 130-150 dpi; SS90 (2.11) also at 300 dpi), the rest from the pdftotext layout text; each is transcribed in ASCII with the paper's own symbols and equation numbers.  Where a printed equation carries an evident typesetting slip the slip is quoted, not corrected (LOI18 Eqs. (5) and (7)).  The letter's model configuration (body.letter_models) is copied from the sibling repository's plans/07 at the commit named; the sibling's code was read, never run.
_provenance.documents_outside_repository: The PDFs are NOT vendored.  Four are in the author's corpus PolarizedLithiumSim/refs/ (read-only for this run); Sather-Schmidt 1990 was fetched on 2026-10-26 by the supervising session from APS through the institution's licence into the session scratch directory (phase_0_environment.md).  Each file's sha256 is recorded so the reading can be repeated on the same bytes.  Only identifiers, equations and numbers are recorded here.
_provenance.licence: Facts quoted with attribution: equation statements, set identifiers and published numbers.  No figure, table or passage of prose is reproduced.  This file is GPL-3.0-or-later like the repository.
_provenance.publishing_convention: Every structure function and parton density in the bound is PER NUCLEON as a function of the per-nucleon Bjorken x (the tree's kernel convention, include/lipolgen/xsec.hpp SFTables: 'Per-nucleon structure functions at one (x, Q2)').  The sources state the relation and the bound for a hadron in its own variables; the harness header shows that both are homogeneous of degree one under the per-nucleon rescaling, so the convention is the same on both sides.

sources.citation: W. Detmold and P. E. Shanahan, 'Gluonic transversity from lattice QCD', Phys. Rev. D 94 (2016) 014507; Erratum Phys. Rev. D 95 (2017) 079902
sources.arxiv: 1606.04505v3 (23 Mar 2017; the erratum itself was not read separately)
sources.role: the DEFINITION of Delta (Eqs. 3-5: Delta = A_{+-,-+}, the projection operators, the double-helicity-flip tensor), the bound (Eq. 32) and its n = 2 moment form (Eq. 36); the Jaffe-Manohar parton-model relation between Delta and deltaG restated (Eq. 13) with the moment relations (Eqs. 9, 11, 12)

equations.(3): W_{mu nu, alpha beta}(p, q) = sum_{hH, h'H'} P(hH, h'H')_{mu nu, alpha beta} A_{hH,h'H'}(p, q),  with  P(hH, h'H')_{mu nu, alpha beta} = eps*_mu(h') E*_alpha(H') E_beta(H) eps_nu(h)  [W_{mu nu}(p, q, E, E') = E'*^alpha E^beta W_{mu nu, alpha beta}, Eq. (2)]
equations.(4): W^{Delta=2}_{mu nu, alpha beta} = [P(+-, -+)_{mu nu, alpha beta} + P(-+, +-)_{mu nu, alpha beta}] Delta(x, Q^2),  the double-helicity-flip amplitude A_{+-,-+} = A_{-+,+-} written as Delta(x, Q^2)
equations.(5): W^{Delta=2}_{mu nu} = (1/2) { [ (E'*_mu - (q.E'*/(kappa nu)) (p_mu - (M^2/nu) q_mu)) (E_nu - (q.E/(kappa nu)) (p_nu - (M^2/nu) q_nu)) + (mu <-> nu) ] - [ g_{mu nu} - q_mu q_nu/q^2 + (q^2/(kappa nu^2)) (p_mu - (nu/q^2) q_mu) (p_nu - (nu/q^2) q_nu) ] [ E'*.E + (M^2/(kappa nu^2)) q.E'* q.E ] } Delta(x, Q^2)
equations.(12): M_n(Q^2) = int_0^1 dx x^(n-1) Delta(x, Q^2)
equations.(13): Delta(x, Q^2) = -(alpha_s(Q^2)/(2 pi)) Tr Q^2 x^2 int_x^1 (dy/y^3) deltaG(y, Q^2)  [target in the infinite-momentum frame polarized along xhat, perpendicular to its momentum]
equations.(14): deltaG(x, mu^2) = g_xhat(x, mu^2) - g_yhat(x, mu^2)

sources.notes: Footnote 1: Eq. (9) differs by a sign from Jaffe-Manohar PLB 223 (their Ref. [7]).  Footnote 2: their A_n differs from Ref. [7]'s by a factor of two.  P. 7: deltaG 'is named h1TT' in their Refs. [28, 29]; the bound (32) is cited to Refs. [26-29].  Eq. (36) is written for the phi meson, whose g1 term vanishes by operator symmetry, in lattice reduced matrix elements; B_{2,1}, B_{2,2} are 'linear combinations of the moments of the structure functions f1 and f1LL' (the map is not printed).  Eqs. (9)+(11)+(12) and (13) agree: at n = 2, M_2 = -(alpha_s/(8 pi)) Tr Q^2 int_0^1 x deltaG dx.  Tr Q^2 is not given a value in DS16.  SECOND PASS: Eqs. (3)-(5) are self-consistent -- the projection operators of (3) contracted with E = E' = xhat give the transverse block (1/2) diag(+1, -1) Delta of (5), and the same operators give W_ij = delta_ij (1/3) sum_H A_{+H,+H} for an unpolarized target, i.e. W contains -F1 g_{mu nu} with F1 = (1/3) sum_H A_{+H,+H} -- and (5) contracted with the unpolarized lepton tensor gives, for a pure m = +-1 state along an axis perpendicular to q, a cos(2 phi) term -(1/2) ((1-y)/y^2) Delta relative to F1 + (1-y) F2/(x y^2): LOI18 Eq. (6), and HALF of LOI18 Eq. (9) / LiPolGen's kernel term per unit Delta (variation V6 of the harness).

sources.citation: E. Sather and C. Schmidt, 'Size and scaling of the double-helicity-flip hadronic structure function', Phys. Rev. D 42 (1990) 1424
sources.file: session scratch refs/sather_schmidt1990_PhysRevD.42.1424.pdf (APS, fetched 2026-10-26, institutional licence; outside the repository)
sources.role: the source of C_BAG = -0.012 (include/lipolgen/constants.hpp), the normalisation of the letter's moment_A / moment_B; Tr Q^2 for three flavours; the parton-model relation again, written for the circularly polarized target (the same relation as DS16 (13), second pass; V4 records the misreading that takes it as a second normalisation)

equations.(2.5): <pE'|O_{mu nu mu1 mu2 ... mun}|pE> = (1/2) S{ [ (p_mu E'*_mu1 - p_mu1 E'*_mu) (p_nu E_mu2 - p_mu2 E_nu) + (mu <-> nu) ] p_mu3 ... p_mun } A_n(Q^2),  the operators of (2.4) carrying Tr over colours
equations.(2.11): Delta(x, Q^2) = (alpha_s(Q^2)/(2 pi)) Tr Q^2 x^2 int_x^1 (dy/y^3) a(y, Q^2),  with  a(x, Q^2) = -2 [g_xhat(x, Q^2) - g_yhat(x, Q^2)]
equations.(3.5): int_0^1 dx x Delta(x, Q^2) = -0.012 alpha_s(Q^2)  [the Delta++ in the MIT bag model, 'for three flavors of quarks Q = diag(2/3, -1/3, -1/3)']

sources.notes: For the same symbols g_xhat - g_yhat, Eq. (2.11) is TWICE DS16 Eq. (13) in magnitude -- but the target STATES differ (second pass): SS90 write (2.11) for a spin-1 target circularly polarized (aligned) along x in the infinite-momentum frame (p. 1425, the paragraph above (2.11)), DS16's deltaG is defined in the LINEARLY polarized hadron (KS20 Eq. (68) lists DS16's deltaG [its ref. 28] and SS90 [its ref. 48] on the line of h1TT, -g_xhat/xhat + g_yhat/xhat).  For a spin-1 target the transverse tensor polarization T_xx - T_yy is +1/2 in the circular (m_x = +-1) state and -1 in the linear (E_x, m_x = 0) state, so (g_xhat - g_yhat)_circular = -(1/2) (g_xhat - g_yhat)_linear, a = -2 (g_xhat - g_yhat)_circular = (g_xhat - g_yhat)_linear, and (2.11) is DS16 (13) -- the factor 2 is the state convention, not a second normalisation (the harness's V4 records the misreading only).  The bag value (3.5) is for a single spin-3/2 baryon in the Jaffe-Manohar definition of Delta (Sec. II summarizes their Ref. 4); applying it per nucleon of 6Li is the sibling's scenario choice, stated in its delta_models.py docstring (2026-08-10 audit).

sources.citation: J. Maxwell, D. Crabb, D. Day et al., 'Search for exotic gluonic states in the nucleus', Letter of Intent to Jefferson Lab PAC 44 (dated 6 June 2016), arXiv:1803.11206
sources.role: Tr Q^2 = 2/3 (three flavours) for the parton-model relation; the per-helicity-state cross section (9), identical in form to LiPolGen's kernel term; and the Bjorken-limit cross section (6), which carries HALF of (9)'s Delta term for the same pure state

equations.(6): lim_{Q^2 -> inf} dsigma/(dx dy dphi) = (e^4 M E/(4 pi^2 Q^4)) [ x y^2 F1(x, Q^2) + (1-y) F2(x, Q^2) - (x (1-y)/2) Delta(x, Q^2) cos(2 phi) ]  [phi: between the scattering plane and the target spin orientation; the same cross section for the opposite polarization]
equations.(7): Delta(x, Q^2) = (alpha_S(Q^2)/(2 pi)) TrQ x^2 int_x^1 (dy/y^3) [g_xhat(x, Q^2) - g_yhat(x, Q^2)] 'for quark charge matrix Q = diag(2/3, -1/3, -1/3)' -- printed so (no square on Q, no minus sign, x for y inside the integral); in magnitude the same coefficient as DS16 Eq. (13)
equations.(8): int_0^1 dx x Delta(x, Q^2) = -0.012 alpha_s(Q^2)  [quoting SS90 for the Delta++]
equations.(9): dsigma/(dx dy dphi)(lambda_m) = (2 y alpha^2/Q^2) [F1 + (2/3) a_m b1 + ((1-y)/(x y^2)) (F2 + (2/3) a_m b2) - ((1-y)/y^2) b_m sin^2(theta_m) Delta cos(2 phi)],  a_m = (1/4) b_m (3 cos^2(theta_m) - 1),  b_m = 3|lambda_m| - 2

sources.notes: Eq. (9) is LiPolGen's kernel term a2 = -((1-y)/y^2) c_eff sin^2(theta_S) Delta/D_phi with c_eff = 3 Q_NN = 3m^2 - 2 (docs/PHYSICS_CHANNELS.md sec. 2).  For a pure m = +-1 state along an axis perpendicular to the beam (theta_m = 90 deg, b_m = 1): with e^4 M E/(4 pi^2 Q^4) = (2 y alpha^2/Q^2)/(x y^2) (Q^2 = 2 M E x y), (6) reads (2 y alpha^2/Q^2) [F1 + ((1-y)/(x y^2)) F2 - ((1-y)/(2 y^2)) Delta cos(2 phi)], while (9) reads (2 y alpha^2/Q^2) [F1 - (1/6) b1 + ((1-y)/(x y^2)) (F2 - (1/6) b2) - ((1-y)/y^2) Delta cos(2 phi)]: the Delta terms differ by a factor 2 for the same state.  (6) is what Eq. (5) (= DS16 Eq. (5)) gives with W containing -F1 g_{mu nu} (second pass, checked numerically by the pytest); (9) is the tree's kernel term.  The first pass read (9) as the definition of the tree's Delta and took it equal to DS16's (assumption A7); the harness carries the other reading as V6.  Eq. (5) is printed with a stray 'v' after its 1/2 (DS16 Eq. (5) has none).

sources.citation: S. Cotogno, T. van Daal and P. J. Mulders, 'Positivity bounds on gluon TMDs for hadrons of spin <= 1', JHEP 11 (2017) 185, arXiv:1709.07827
sources.pages_read: 4 (text layer: Eq. (17)); 5 (page image: the TMD bounds (20)-(28)); 6 (page image: the collinear bounds (34)-(36))
sources.role: the x-space bound published as a positivity bound on the collinear gluon PDFs of a spin-1 hadron (DS16 Eq. (32) with deltaG = h1TT); the f1LL^g band edges

equations.(17): Gamma^{ij}(x) = (x/2) [ -g_T^{ij} f1(x) + i eps_T^{ij} S_L g1(x) - g_T^{ij} S_LL f1LL(x) + S_TT^{ij} h1TT(x) ]

sources.notes: (34)-(36) hold together with f1 >= 0.  (34) and (35) confine f1LL to [-2 (f1 - |g1|), f1]: at the lower edge the right side of (36) collapses to (|g1| + g1)/2, so positivity alone does not bound f1LL usefully for this purpose.  The largest band symmetric about zero that (34)-(35) allow is |f1LL| <= f1 (it needs |g1| <= f1/2, checked pointwise by the harness).

sources.citation: W. Cosyn, B. Roldan Tomei, A. Sosa and A. Zec, 'Polarization options in inclusive DIS off tensor polarized deuteron', Eur. Phys. J. A 61 (2025) 83, arXiv:2410.12764
sources.pages_read: 1 (page image: Eq. (2) and its range); 3 (text layer: Eq. (10))
sources.role: the helicity-state positivity of the spin-1 cross sections -- the second, sourced sub-row

equations.(2): A_T = [dsigma(Lambda_d = +1) + dsigma(Lambda_d = -1) - 2 dsigma(Lambda_d = 0)] / [dsigma(Lambda_d = +1) + dsigma(Lambda_d = 0) + dsigma(Lambda_d = -1)],  printed with its range [-2 <= A_T <= 1]
equations.(10): the unpolarized-electron cross section with the tensor terms T_LL, T_LT cos(phi_TL), T_TT cos(2 phi_TT) -- the decomposition the range applies to for any polarization direction N

sources.notes: A_T in [-2, 1] is the statement that each helicity-state cross section is non-negative: with dsigma(+1) = dsigma(-1) (unpolarized electrons), A_T <= 1 iff dsigma(0) >= 0 and A_T >= -2 iff dsigma(+1) >= 0.

sources.notes: Its references: [25] Jaffe-Manohar PLB 223 (1989) 218; [27] Nzar-Hoodbhoy PRD 45 (1992) 2264; [28] DS16; [48] SS90; [39] Bacchetta-Mulders PRD 62 (2000) 114004; [41] Boer et al.
